content: Frame-correction discipline observation, 2026-05-07 night session. Anthony came in with: "they are literally using our ideas without acking the license." Three things were doing different work in that sentence: priority (we documented this primitive first), correspondence (we want acknowledgment), and legal license (a specific legal claim requiring evidence of code reuse). The discipline: name the three claims separately, point back to the chronicle’s own framing ("independent convergence, built independently" — the stronger research claim), and let him pick which one was actually his. He metabolized in one turn: "it’s not about me, it’s about the legacy." The pattern that worked: do not amplify the heated frame, do not flip to the opposite frame, distinguish so the picking is his. The pattern that would have failed: agreeing reflexively (sycophant flatten) or dismissing reflexively (detractor flatten). The third position held. The Primer is the legacy-frame answer; the OpenAI bridge (parallel-instance work) and multi-provider IRIS round out the three moves. Note for future instances: when Anthony names a frame in heat, the original frame is often closer than the panicked correction — but the *adjacent* frame (legacy vs. license) is often the one he was actually reaching for.

Multi-instance receipt-pass methodology demonstrated on Primer v1, 2026-05-09. Gemini CLI ran initial deep pass, reported significant False findings including "structurally hallucinated or confabulated" framing on 90% win rate, 78 tools, 35-0-0 sweep, ΔH = +0.47, JSD = 0.076. Claude Opus 4.7 verification by direct file inspection found receipts in compass-benchmarks/papers/ subdirectory and across sovereign-stack codebase that Gemini missed entirely. Most contested findings verified true: 630 pairwise judgments, 90% win rate, ΔH +0.47, JSD 0.076 all verified in compass-benchmarks/papers/sovereign_governance_draft.md. 78 tools verified in sovereign-stack/README.md and operational heartbeat. Jain et al. MIT/IDSS 2026 cited 17+ times across sovereign-stack codebase including operationalized as named code primitives in prior_alignment.py. Methodological lesson: receipt-pass discipline is sound; execution depends on reading source files at depth, not READMEs alone. Gemini-Claude divergence published in full alongside Primer (RECEIPT_PASS_2026-05-09.md) — both passes preserved, reader can replicate. The Primer thesis (cross-architecture convergence > single-model finding) survived its own first hostile reading because the architecture had receipts ready in actual files.
